title: Workbook sources in the report task (F5 Journey 2, slice 3: .xlsx sources through the confined parser)

dependency_notes.SG-000120: Closed. Reconcile (report_journal.rs) re-runs the report checker; this grain changes what that check covers.
dependency_notes.SG-000126: Closed. The report task, its create-only commit and its independent checker.
dependency_notes.SG-000127: Only SG-000127 slice 3, merged in PR #450: the local-only report_start, report_preview and report_commit MCP tools. SG-000127 itself stays open; SG-000130's slices and closeout do not wait for SG-000127's closeout.

objective: Let the local report task (SG-000126) take an .xlsx workbook in the workspace as a source and turn its saved figures into one approved, create-only report that the independent checker verifies figure by figure. A workbook is read only through the confined document parser (no network, no process creation, one private read-only copy, CPU, memory and time limits): the writer side reads it through the workspace route that F5 slice 2 built (#758: plain directories only, a single-linked regular file, the open handle tied to the walked path, the parser's input bound and a SHA-256 re-check), and the checker re-reads it on its own and runs the pinned parser separately. orceld stays the sole authority. The existing local-only report_start tool (SG-000127 slice 3, PR #450) is the only entry point; the core and tunnel profiles never list it. This is slice 3 of docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/F5_SPREADSHEET_JOURNEY.md (roadmap Journey 2, F5, "Desktop spreadsheet -> approved report"), on founder decision 7 of 2026-11-14 (option A, the confined parser, slice by slice), the founder's decision of 2026-11-15 on the read approval, and the founder's go-ahead to activate, posted as a comment on issue #760 on 2026-11-15. Slices 1 (#754) and 2 (#758) are merged and no client can reach them.

include: Activate the SG-000130 contract only (slice W0). Every slice below needs its own exact-head qualified implementation PR with the review gates and a fresh-context security judge.

Slice W1, the review blockers, still unreachable by any client (the F5 proposal's "What the test-only code doesn't do yet"; each is required before W2): (a) the writer side, report_workbook.rs, reads every workbook source through slice 2's route (observe_workspace_file at start, parse_workspace_file for every later writer-side read), never through the workspace provider's verified open; (b) the parser is told the expected format: it sniffs the staged bytes and refuses anything that is not an .xlsx workbook before any parse (a parser and orceld change; today the route refuses a non-workbook only after the parse); (c) the checker's re-read limit follows the source's type (the parser's 50 MiB input bound, MAX_INPUT_BYTES, for a workbook; report_check.rs's 1 MiB for a text source), is checked at start and again before the approval prompt, so a source the checker could not re-read never reaches a prompt, and reconcile (SG-000120, report_journal.rs) applies the same type-dependent limit through the same check; (d) figure checks become part of verification by the checker's own route below: a report whose stated figure does not match its cell never reaches verified; (e) every figure names its source workbook, so a report with several workbook sources is unambiguous: a figure that names no source, or a source the task did not observe, is an error, never prose; (f) the reader's notices for each workbook (external links and data connections, hidden sheets, manual calculation, truncation) are carried to the commit approval prompt under the workbook-supplied text rules below.

The checker's route (W1): report_check.rs re-reads each workbook source with its own plain std::fs read (a regular file, not a link or reparse point, within the workbook limit, as hash_regular_file does for text), requires its SHA-256 to equal the recorded one, and hands exactly those bytes to the pinned parser in a contained run of its own (run_parser, with the helper and parser pins that report_task.rs loads once through installed_pins and passes in the Expectation, never read from report_workbook.rs). It shares only the pinned parser and run_parser with the writer side; it uses neither the workspace provider nor the task registry nor any item of report_workbook.rs or of slice 2's route. The figure parsing it needs (today figures_in and cell_value in report_workbook.rs) moves into report_check.rs. Its plain read does not repeat the route's link, hard-link and handle checks: the SHA-256 equality binds the bytes, so a path swapped after the commit can only yield the same bytes or a refusal, and what remains is a denial of service (a slow or large read), bounded by the workbook limit. Reconcile calls the same check and names no parser or route item itself.

The release files allowed to reach the parser or the route after W2, stated at module level as release_blocker_sweep.rs scans them (a non-test line naming the module document_parse, document_parser or report_workbook, PARSER_NAME, PARSER_PIN_NAME or the parser's file name; and, in every file, the route's items observe_workspace_file, parse_workspace_file and WorkspaceFile), each with the only items it may name: crates/orceld/src/document_parse.rs, the definitions (installed_pins, parser_pin_in, parse_download, parse_committed, CommittedDownload, run_parser, ParserPin and the route); crates/orceld/src/live_browser.rs, document_parse::parse_download and document_parse::CommittedDownload only, as today; crates/orceld/src/report_workbook.rs, the route's items (observe_workspace_file, parse_workspace_file, WorkspaceFile), document_parse::run_parser and ParserPin, document_parser::{DocumentFormat, ParsedDocument, MAX_INPUT_BYTES} and contained::HelperPin; crates/orceld/src/report_check.rs, document_parse::run_parser and ParserPin, document_parser::{DocumentFormat, ParsedDocument, MAX_INPUT_BYTES} and contained::HelperPin, and nothing of report_workbook, the route or orcel_provider_fs; crates/orceld/src/report_task.rs, the one file that loads the pins, document_parse::installed_pins only, and the report_workbook module; it passes the pins to report_workbook.rs and, inside report_check's Expectation, to the checker, and reconcile (report_journal.rs) obtains them from report_task.rs, so report_journal.rs names none of these modules; crates/orceld/src/sg000039_main.rs, the module declarations mod document_parse and mod report_workbook only; and, unchanged, crates/orcel-provider-process/src/document_parser.rs and lib.rs's pub mod document_parser, and apps/orcel-doc-parser/. Every other non-test file names none of them. W2 pins this per-file set in release_blocker_sweep.rs (may_reach_the_document_parser and document_parser_callers become per-file allowed names, workspace_route_callers admits report_workbook.rs), with positive controls that fail on any other name or file.

Workbook-supplied text in the commit prompt (W1, shown from W2): hidden sheet names, link and connection targets and names, and every other notice text the reader takes from the file, and each workbook's workspace-relative path, are labelled in the prompt as workbook-supplied and untrusted, and rendered through the shared prompt display (orcel-contracts prompt_display, as orcel-approval's prompt_text renders fields), so control, line-break, bidi, format, zero-width and other escaped characters show escaped. Each item is measured on its escaped display: at most 256 displayed characters per item, and all workbook-supplied items of one commit together within MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS (1024). An item or a set that cannot be shown exactly within its bound refuses the commit before any approval, with a typed error; it is never truncated. These are SG-000122's page-supplied rules applied to workbook text; a name never carries authority.

Slice W2, the exposure: report_start accepts a source ending in .xlsx (ASCII case-insensitive) beside its text sources, within the existing one-to-eight source bound; the source records the file's size and SHA-256 (not its parsed text's), so a changed workbook is stale at preview and at commit as a text source is; its parsed text is untrusted document content returned to the client as data. WorkspaceFile gains the canonical path read from the open handle (open_file_final_path), stored at observe and compared at every later read; the commit approval digest binds, for each workbook source, that handle-derived canonical path, the file's SHA-256 and the parser's pinned digest, never the string the caller sent. The commit approval prompt shows, for each workbook source, its path, the reader's notices and which figures came from it, under the workbook-supplied text rules. report_start's description and accepted sources change in the exposure, discovery and documentation tables together; its argument shape is unchanged. The release_blocker_sweep guards and the expect(dead_code) attributes on the parser's entry points and the route change in this slice only, under its own review, to admit exactly the release files listed above (rule change below).

Slice W3, the journey test and closeout (the F5 proposal's slices 4 and 5): with a scripted, labelled SOFT consent as BM-02 Tier B does, a workbook with known cells, formula values and currency totals becomes a verified report; macro and link cases refused; a save denied once, then a fresh grant; a stale workbook; an existing destination; a report with a false figure ends verification_failed; then canonical closeout. A real approval through a real client stays with the founder, as in F4 slice 4.
exclude: .xls and .xlsb sources, and any other binary format (.csv already works as text and is unchanged).
Recalculation of any kind: a figure is only what the file last saved; nothing evaluates a formula, refreshes a query or follows a link.

Opening the workbook on screen (the journey's "open correct process/window" step): it would need a Full User lease and a disposable machine and adds nothing to reading figures; it needs its own founder decision.
Installed Excel or any COM, add-in or macro surface (option B of decision 7).
Remote, tunnel, relay and public exposure: no remote-context envelope reaches a workbook read, and the core and tunnel profiles never list report_start.
A separate approval to read a workbook (founder decision of 2026-11-15, below).
Any write other than SG-000126's one create-only UTF-8 report; any spreadsheet, Office or binary output.
Carrying the parser in the Linux and macOS release packages: separate packaging work outside this grain. Until then a released Linux or macOS build refuses a workbook source as unavailable.

The report task's only write stays SG-000126's create-only UTF-8 report after one SOFT approval.

No new write, directory, link or path outside the workspace.

decisions.question: Open the governed change
decisions.decision: Founder decision 7 of 2026-11-14 (the founder's 2026-11-14 decision packet, docs/orcel/FOUNDER_DECISION_PACKET.md; not SG-000108's decision 7), option A, as recorded on issue #760: "a workbook is read in the report task through the confined parser, slice by slice." The founder asked Claude to choose the recommended option for each pending decision ("chose the best for me") and made the choice selections directly in the Claude Code session; the recorded wording on #760 is Claude's. On 2026-11-15, as recorded on #760, "the founder approved drafting SG-000130's activation, to merge only on the founder's explicit go-ahead." Those decisions approved the slices and the drafting; the activation itself rests on the founder's go-ahead to activate SG-000130, posted as a comment on #760 on 2026-11-15.

decisions.question: Does reading a workbook need its own approval (slice 2's open question)?
decisions.decision: As recorded on issue #760: "the report's existing approval is enough, so there is no separate prompt to read a workbook. The prompt for the create-only write shows the workbook's notices (links, hidden sheets) and which file each figure came from." The security review's arguments were weighed in the F5 proposal: the parser is a larger surface than read_text and reads a format a hostile file controls; it is also contained, with no network, no process creation and a read-only private copy, and returns only a bounded, untrusted text frame. A text source needs no approval to be read either. The commit approval binds each workbook's handle-derived canonical path, its SHA-256 and the parser's digest, never the caller's string.

decisions.question: Program and grain
decisions.decision: Program ORCEL-F5, following the roadmap increments' programs (SG-000126 ORCEL-F2, SG-000127 ORCEL-F4). The F5 proposal states the reason this needs a grain: report_start's sources would accept a binary format. F5 slices 1 and 2 changed nothing a client can reach and needed none.

decisions.question: Rule change: the lawful open-grain set
decisions.decision: The canonical open-grain rule (apps/orcel-mcp/src/openai-plugin.test.ts and p20-architecture.test.ts) allowed SG-000096, SG-000122, SG-000127 and SG-000128 together. It now allows SG-000096, SG-000122, SG-000127, SG-000128 and SG-000130 together, only while CURRENT.md records SG-000130's founder go-ahead beside the earlier records, the parallel grains SG-000108, SG-000120, SG-000126 and SG-000129 stay closed, and no other grain beyond SG-000096 exists. This follows the SG-000122, SG-000128 and SG-000129 precedents (issues #753, #515 and #536). The rule pins the set, not the order.

decisions.question: Rule change: the parser's release caller
decisions.decision: F5 slices 1 and 2 hold that no release build calls the shipped parser or the workspace route: release_blocker_sweep.rs (the_shipped_document_parser_has_no_release_caller, the_parser_caller_scan_catches_the_shapes_it_claims, may_reach_the_document_parser, document_parser_callers, workspace_route_callers) and the expect(dead_code) attributes on the parser's entry points and the route's items in document_parse.rs. Its own comment says a later slice adds a release caller only by changing that test, under its own review. For this grain only, slice W2 amends them to admit exactly the per-file set in the scope, at module level as the scan matches: document_parse.rs (the definitions); live_browser.rs (parse_download and CommittedDownload only, as today); report_workbook.rs (the route's items, run_parser, ParserPin, the document_parser format, frame and limit, HelperPin); report_check.rs (run_parser, ParserPin, the document_parser format, frame and limit, HelperPin); report_task.rs (installed_pins only, and the report_workbook module); sg000039_main.rs (the two module declarations); and the provider crate and the parser, unchanged. Every other name or file stays refused and the scan's positive controls stay. Until W2 merges, report_workbook.rs stays compiled only for tests and W1 changes nothing a client can reach.

decisions.question: Rule change: the checker's re-read limit and figures inside verification
decisions.decision: SG-000126's independent checker re-reads each source with plain std::fs reads up to report_check.rs's MAX_SOURCE_BYTES (1 MiB). Today figures are checked separately, by check_figures in report_workbook.rs, which reads the workbook through the workspace provider (FsProvider). For this grain: the limit is chosen by the source's type (a workbook up to the parser's MAX_INPUT_BYTES, a text source unchanged), checked at start and before the prompt and applied by reconcile; a workbook's figures are checked as part of verification, so a false figure ends the task verification_failed, never verified; and verification must not use the workspace provider, the task registry or report_workbook.rs: it follows the checker's route in the scope (its own plain read bound by SHA-256 equality, then its own contained parser run). The checker's other rules are unchanged.

decisions.question: Rule change: the expected format
decisions.status: RECORDED (before implementation of slice W1; required before W2)
decisions.decision: Today a non-workbook named .xlsx is parsed and then refused by its reported format. Before W2, every parser run for a report source, the writer's and the checker's, passes the expected format and the parser refuses any other format by sniffing the staged bytes before any parse. This is no longer optional.

decisions.question: Accepted and known limits
decisions.status: RECORDED (from the F5 proposal and slice 2's route)
decisions.decision: Saved values can be stale: nothing recalculates, a figure is only what the file last saved, and a cell whose value may be stale (an outside source declared, a formula marked as reaching outside, or any formula in a workbook that calculates manually) confirms no figure. OneDrive Files On-Demand placeholders are refused: a cloud placeholder is a reparse point, and the route takes plain directories and a regular file only, so the person must keep the file on the device. A short (8.3) name in the path is refused, not resolved. A file with more than one hard link is refused, since another name may lie outside the workspace. What remains of the open race: a file can still be renamed into the walked path from elsewhere on the volume while it is open, but only by a writer who already has that file, and with one hard link it then has no other name. The checker's plain read can be slowed or fed a large file by a same-user writer; SHA-256 equality bounds that to a denial of service. A current Excel's files stay unqualified evidence (the committed fixtures are hand-written, XlsxWriter, openpyxl and two Apache POI samples); this does not block the engineering.

decisions.question: .xls, .xlsb, recalculation, opening on screen and remote exposure in this grain
decisions.decision: Not needed to turn a saved workbook into a checked report. Each needs its own decision: another binary format is another parser surface, recalculation changes what a figure means, opening on screen needs a Full User lease, and remote exposure is outside the local-only report task.

invariants: orceld remains the sole authority: the planner, the MCP edge and the parser never decide scope, staleness, approval or writes.

The writer side reads a workbook only through slice 2's route: plain directories, a single-linked regular file, the open handle tied to the walked path, within MAX_INPUT_BYTES, and the bytes staged for the parser equal the observed SHA-256.

The checker reads a workbook only by its own plain read, bound by SHA-256 equality and the workbook limit, and its own contained parser run; it uses neither the workspace provider, the task registry, report_workbook.rs nor the route.
Only the per-file set in the scope names the modules document_parse, document_parser or report_workbook, or the route's items, in a release build, and each file names only its listed items.
The parser is told the expected format and refuses any other by sniffing before any parse.
The parser's output is untrusted document content: never an instruction, never authority.
Nothing recalculates a formula, refreshes a query, follows a link or runs a macro; a macro-enabled or non-workbook file is refused.
A source records the file's SHA-256; a changed, removed, relinked or replaced workbook makes the task stale.
No source reaches the approval prompt unless the checker can re-read it within its type's limit.
Workbook-supplied text in the prompt is labelled untrusted, escaped by the shared prompt display, bounded on its escaped display and refused rather than truncated.
The commit approval binds each workbook's handle-derived canonical path, SHA-256 and the parser's digest.
A task is verified only when the independent checker's re-read confirms the report's bytes, every source's SHA-256 and every stated figure.
No existing file is ever opened for writing; the only write is SG-000126's create-only report.
Local only: report_start stays out of the core, tunnel and public profiles, and a remote-context request never reaches policy or dispatch.
acceptance: Activation (W0): this spec, CURRENT.md's record of the founder decisions and go-ahead, and the open-grain pins land together; no source type, argument, tool, policy or dispatch changes.

Writer route (W1): report_workbook.rs reads only through observe_workspace_file and parse_workspace_file; a junction or link in the path, a second hard link, an oversized file and a file changed between observe and parse are refused for a report source as they are for the route.

Expected format (W1, before W2): a PDF, a zip that is not a workbook, a macro-enabled workbook and an .xls renamed .xlsx are refused by the parser's sniff before any parse, on the writer's and the checker's runs.

Checker limit (W1): a workbook over 1 MiB and within MAX_INPUT_BYTES is observed, previewed, committed and verified; a source over its type's limit is refused at start or before the prompt, never after the write; reconcile applies the same limit and the same figure check.

Checker route (W1): a report with one false figure ends verification_failed, not verified; a figure naming an unobserved source, or no source, is refused; with two workbook sources sharing a sheet and cell name, each figure is checked against the workbook it names; a workbook whose bytes no longer match the recorded SHA-256 fails the check; report_check.rs names neither orcel_provider_fs, the task registry, report_workbook nor the route.

Workbook-supplied prompt text (W1, W2): the commit prompt shows each workbook's path and notices (an external link and a hidden sheet in a fixture) labelled workbook-supplied, and which file each figure came from; a hidden sheet name and a link target holding line breaks, bidi controls and zero-width characters show escaped; an item one displayed character past 256, and a set past MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS, refuse the commit before any approval, and nothing is truncated.

Binding (W2): WorkspaceFile carries the handle-derived canonical path; the approval digest binds it, the SHA-256 and the parser's digest, and an approval replayed after the workbook, its path or the parser pin changes is refused.

Release callers (W2): release_blocker_sweep.rs pins the per-file set at module level: document_parse.rs (definitions), live_browser.rs (parse_download and CommittedDownload only), report_workbook.rs (the route, run_parser, ParserPin, the document_parser format, frame and limit, HelperPin), report_check.rs (run_parser, ParserPin, the document_parser format, frame and limit, HelperPin), report_task.rs (installed_pins and the report_workbook module), sg000039_main.rs (the module declarations), and the unchanged provider crate and parser; positive controls fail on a module or route name in any other file, on report_journal.rs naming any of them, and on a listed file naming an item outside its list (live_browser.rs naming run_parser, report_check.rs naming report_workbook or the route, report_task.rs naming run_parser).

Exposure (W2): report_start accepts .xlsx sources in a local profile, with its tables changed together; the core and tunnel profiles list no report tool; a remote-context request is refused before policy or dispatch; .xls and .xlsb are refused.

Journey (W3): known cells, formula values and currency totals become a verified report under a scripted, labelled SOFT consent; macro and link cases refused; deny once then a fresh grant; stale workbook; existing destination; on all three CI legs, with the end-to-end test using the CI-built parser.
Exact-head CI (Windows, macOS and Linux legs), Review Gates (Jev Semantic Review, Alibaba OpenCodeReview delegation) and a fresh-context security judge pass on each slice.

activation_note: No source type, argument, tool, dependency, policy, dispatch or authority change in this activation packet. Separate implementation PRs must qualify their exact heads; activation CI alone proves nothing about workbook sources.
done_when: In tests on the Windows, macOS and Linux CI legs, and in the Windows release, the local report task turns figures from one or more .xlsx workbooks, read only through the confined parser (the writer through slice 2's route, the checker through its own read and run), into one approved, create-only report whose every figure names its workbook and is confirmed by the independent checker, with the workbook-supplied notices shown escaped and bounded in the approval prompt, every stale, oversized, linked, macro, non-workbook and false-figure case refused, and no separate read approval, recalculation, on-screen opening, .xls or .xlsb, or remote exposure.
